reviews.decision_reason: select_demand appears to preserve the target corpus needs exactly: all eight input records are present in assigned_job_output.needs with the same record_id, need, demand_score, source_id, and source_weight. There is no visible defect localized to this unit in the supplied semantic package.

normalize_evidence is the behaviorally significant fault. It ranks evidence_sources in reverse market-demand order: the lowest demand/weight record n06-r08 is rank 1, while the strongest demand record n06-r01 is rank 8. That corrupted handoff is then reflected downstream: the final priorities choose unsupported n06-r07 over unsupported n06-r01, producing the wrong top_need despite n06-r01 having the strongest demand_score and source_weight.

assemble_provenance appears to pass through the normalized records and metadata without an additional visible defect. The incorrect downstream recommendation is explained by the already-corrupted evidence ranking from normalize_evidence, not by a separate provenance assembly failure in the supplied package.
